questions.question: What does CSS stand for?
questions.explanation: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) controls the visual presentation of HTML elements — colors, layout, fonts, spacing, and animations.

questions.question: What is CSS specificity?
options: The order in which CSS files are loaded
A ranking system that determines which CSS rule wins when multiple rules target the same element
The number of CSS properties applied
questions.correct_answer: A ranking system that determines which CSS rule wins when multiple rules target the same element
questions.explanation: Specificity hierarchy: inline styles > IDs > classes/attributes/pseudo-classes > element selectors. Higher specificity wins.

questions.question: What does 'display: flex' do to a container?
options: Enables Flexbox layout so children are arranged in a flexible row or column
questions.correct_answer: Enables Flexbox layout so children are arranged in a flexible row or column
questions.explanation: display:flex turns the element into a flex container. Direct children become flex items and can be aligned, sized, and ordered flexibly.

questions.question: What does 'justify-content: space-between' do in Flexbox?
options: Places first item at start, last at end, equal space between others
Adds equal space around all items
Stretches items to fill the container
questions.correct_answer: Places first item at start, last at end, equal space between others
questions.explanation: space-between distributes items with no space at the edges. space-around adds equal space on both sides; space-evenly for all gaps.

questions.question: What is the CSS Box Model?
options: The content + padding + border + margin layers that make up every element
questions.correct_answer: The content + padding + border + margin layers that make up every element
questions.explanation: Every HTML element is a box. From inside out: content area, padding (space inside border), border, margin (space outside border).

questions.question: What does 'box-sizing: border-box' do?
options: Makes width/height include padding and border in the calculation
Sets the border to a box shape
questions.correct_answer: Makes width/height include padding and border in the calculation
questions.explanation: With border-box, setting width:300px means the element is 300px total including padding and border — making layout math easier.

questions.question: Which CSS property controls the stacking order of positioned elements?
questions.explanation: z-index controls the stack order of positioned elements (position: relative/absolute/fixed/sticky). Higher value = in front.

questions.question: What does 'position: absolute' do?
options: Positions relative to the viewport always
Removes element from flow, positions relative to nearest positioned ancestor
questions.correct_answer: Removes element from flow, positions relative to nearest positioned ancestor
questions.explanation: absolute removes the element from normal flow and positions it relative to the nearest ancestor with position other than static.

questions.question: What is the purpose of CSS Grid's 'grid-template-columns'?
options: Defines the column structure and sizes for a grid container
questions.correct_answer: Defines the column structure and sizes for a grid container
questions.explanation: grid-template-columns defines how many columns the grid has and their sizes. E.g., 'repeat(3, 1fr)' creates 3 equal columns.

questions.question: What does 'fr' unit mean in CSS Grid?
questions.explanation: 1fr means 1 fraction of the available space. '1fr 2fr' creates two columns where the second is twice as wide as the first.

questions.question: What does '@media (max-width: 768px)' do?
options: Applies styles only when viewport is 768px wide or narrower
questions.correct_answer: Applies styles only when viewport is 768px wide or narrower
questions.explanation: Media queries apply CSS conditionally based on viewport size. max-width: 768px targets tablets and mobile devices.

questions.question: What is the 'cascade' in Cascading Style Sheets?
options: The algorithm that determines which CSS rules apply when multiple rules target the same element
questions.correct_answer: The algorithm that determines which CSS rules apply when multiple rules target the same element
questions.explanation: The cascade considers specificity, origin (browser/user/author), and source order to determine which rule wins for each property.

questions.question: What does 'transition: all 0.3s ease' do?
options: Animates all CSS property changes over 0.3 seconds with ease timing
questions.correct_answer: Animates all CSS property changes over 0.3 seconds with ease timing
questions.explanation: transition creates smooth animations for CSS property changes (like hover effects). ease starts slow, speeds up, then slows down.

questions.question: What is the difference between em and rem units?
options: em is relative to the root font size; rem is relative to the parent element
em is relative to the parent element; rem is relative to the root (html) font size
questions.correct_answer: em is relative to the parent element; rem is relative to the root (html) font size
questions.explanation: em scales relative to the parent, causing compound scaling in nested elements. rem always references the root html font-size — more predictable.

questions.question: What does 'overflow: hidden' do?
options: Clips content that extends beyond the element's boundaries
questions.correct_answer: Clips content that extends beyond the element's boundaries
questions.explanation: overflow:hidden hides any content that overflows the element box. Useful for card layouts, image cropping, and clearing floats.
